ABOUT TIPPING...
How did the word "Tip" originate? Accord-
ing to legend it was derived from the initial
letters of the phrase "To Insure Promptness."
Boxes were set up in English Inns during the
18th Century and imprinted with the above
phrase. This was to remind the guests that a
coin deposited in these boxes would bring
special service. Later the phrase was ab-
breviated to T. I. P.
Aboard the Pan American Flying Clippers, a
Tip—To Insure Promptness-is not neces-
sary. Your Purser will be happy to give you
prompt, courteous service.

properties.sfomuseum:description: Flight information packet issued by Pan American World Airways, titled "Your adventure in the Pacific," comprising:a. folder; tri-fold format with three pockets;b. brochure titled "Flying Clipper-wise"; multipage booklet;c. bar service menu; quad-fold format;d. timetable for transpacific flights, effective November 1949; fold-out format; includes shipping rates for cargo;e. time selector; two round cards attached at center; used to determine time in other zones;f. postcard with full color photographic image of of Wat Benchamabopit [Marble Temple] in Bangkok.
